subject: general
question: An open metallic box is 60 cm long, 40 cm wide and 23 cm high. Its thickness is 3 cm. If 1 cm³ of metal used in the box weighs 0.5 grams, find the weight (in kg) of the box.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the box is open at the top, thickness is deducted twice from length and width, but only once from height.

Inner dimensions: l = 60 − 6 = 54 cm, w = 40 − 6 = 34 cm, h = 23 − 3 = 20 cm.

Volume of metal = Outer Volume − Inner Volume

⇒ Volume = (60 × 40 × 23) − (54 × 34 × 20)

⇒ Volume = 55200 − 36720 = 18480 cm³

⇒ Weight = (18480 × 0.5) / 1000 = 9.24 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 9.24 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Outer length (L) = 60 cm

Outer width (W) = 40 cm

Outer height (H) = 23 cm

Thickness (t) = 3 cm

Weight of 1 cm³ metal = 0.5 grams

**Formula Used:**

Inner length (l) = L − 2t

Inner width (w) = W − 2t

Inner height (h) = H − t (since the box is open at the top)

Volume of metal = Outer Volume − Inner Volume = (L × W × H) − (l × w × h)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Inner length (l) = 60 − 2 × 3 = 60 − 6 = 54 cm

⇒ Inner width (w) = 40 − 2 × 3 = 40 − 6 = 34 cm

⇒ Inner height (h) = 23 − 3 = 20 cm

⇒ Outer Volume = 60 × 40 × 23 = 55200 cm³

⇒ Inner Volume = 54 × 34 × 20 = 36720 cm³

⇒ Volume of metal used = 55200 − 36720 = 18480 cm³

⇒ Total Weight = 18480 × 0.5 = 9240 grams

⇒ Total Weight in kg = 9240 ÷ 1000 = 9.24 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 9.24 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Open vs Closed Box Dimensions

For a completely closed box of uniform thickness t, the inner dimensions are obtained by subtracting 2t from all outer dimensions (L, W, H). For an open box, 2t is subtracted from length and width, but only t is subtracted from the height.

Volume and Capacity

The external volume calculates the total space the box occupies. The internal volume is the capacity of the box (how much it can hold).

Density and Mass Relation

Mass = Volume × Density. Always ensure consistent units before performing multiplication. For instance, if density is given in grams per cm³, volume must be in cm³ before calculating the final mass.
